params.help: A .ltb bundle: the encoder, the task head and the thresholds it was validated with. One bundle serves planes, volumes, multi-channel stacks and clips
params.label: Model

params.help: Segment gives objects with extents; Detect gives one voxel per object, which is faster and is what the model predicts directly; Track follows objects across time and needs more than one time point
params.label: Task

params.help: The model accepts several channels at once. Send all of them only when the bundle was trained with channel identities, otherwise pick one
params.label: Channels

params.help: Peak probability cut. 0 uses the value the bundle was validated at
params.label: Threshold

params.help: Two peaks closer than this are one object. In microns, so it means the same thing on anisotropic data. 0 uses the bundle's value
params.label: Min. separation

params.help: Drop smaller objects (0 = keep all)
params.label: Min. voxels

params.help: Inference tile (z, y, x); a zero extent uses the bundle's own crop size on that axis
params.label: Tile

params.help: A TorchScript / ONNX file taking (1, 1, Z, Y, X) float32, or a spec the worker resolves: hf:<repo>[:<file>] (Hugging Face, cached in $SIRIUS_MODEL_CACHE or ~/.sirius/models), cellpose:<model> (default = the installed Cellpose's built-in model, one of its model names, or a custom model file) or microsam:<model_type> (vit_b_lm, vit_l_lm, vit_t_lm, vit_b_em_organelles, ...). Cellpose and micro-SAM return instance labels directly; threshold and post-processing then do not apply
params.label: Model

params.help: Tile extent (z, y, x); must fit GPU memory
params.label: Tile

params.help: Tile halo; should exceed the model's receptive-field radius
params.label: Overlap

params.help: Foreground probability cut
params.label: Threshold

params.help: Drop smaller objects (0 = keep all)
params.label: Min. voxels

params.help: Minimum distance between watershed seeds
params.label: Seed distance

params.help: Manual threshold
params.label: Value

params.help: Before anything else: a 3x3 median drops shot noise without moving an edge; Perona-Malik diffusion smooths the inside of a region and leaves its boundary alone
params.label: Denoise

params.help: Anisotropic diffusion: more steps, smoother interiors
params.label: Diffusion steps

params.help: Anisotropic diffusion: a gradient this large, as a fraction of the intensity range, counts as an edge and is kept
params.label: Diffusion edge

params.help: What to bring out before the threshold: round objects of one size, tubes of a range of widths, or the thinnest lines of all
params.label: Enhance

params.help: Blobs: the radius they respond to. Tubes: the smallest tube width
params.label: Feature σ

params.help: Tubes: the largest width; the response is the best over the range
params.label: Feature σ max

params.help: Tubes: how many widths between the two σ
params.label: Scales

params.help: How the background is estimated before it is subtracted. The box top-hat follows a flat background; the rolling ball follows a curved one, which is what uneven illumination or a thick specimen actually gives
params.label: Background

params.help: Structures larger than this radius are background and are removed (0 = off)
params.label: Background radius

params.help: Gaussian blur before the threshold (0 = none)
params.label: Smoothing σ

params.help: Otsu splits the histogram in two; Triangle suits the skewed histogram of a mostly empty field, where Otsu cuts too high; Li keeps dim objects; the local rules follow an uneven background
params.label: Threshold

params.help: Manual threshold
params.label: Value

params.help: Local mean: side of the neighbourhood the mean is taken over
params.label: Local window

params.help: Local mean: foreground where value > ratio × local mean + offset
params.label: Local ratio

params.help: Local contrast: the cut sits k local standard deviations above the local mean, so it follows both the background level and the local noise
params.label: Contrast k

params.help: Keep everything connected to what is clearly above the cut, down to a lower one. A filament that fades stays whole instead of breaking into pieces
params.label: Hysteresis

params.help: Where the lower cut sits between the image floor and the threshold: 0.5 is halfway, 1 turns hysteresis off
params.label: Hysteresis low

params.help: Morphological Chan-Vese: moves the mask boundary to the best two-region fit of the image. It has no shape assumption, so it suits filaments as well as cells, and it repairs a threshold that leaked or pinched
params.label: Refine

params.help: Curvature rounds per step; more gives a smoother contour
params.label: Refine smoothing

params.help: Binary opening drops specks and necks thinner than this (0 = off)
params.label: Opening radius

params.help: Enclosed background inside an object becomes object, per plane
params.label: Fill holes

params.help: Background the object encloses in three dimensions becomes object. A cavity no single plane closes is invisible to the per-plane fill, which is most of them in a stack
params.label: Fill holes (3D)

params.help: 3D fill: leave cavities larger than this open (0 = fill them all), so a real lumen survives
params.label: Largest hole

params.help: How the mask becomes objects. The distance watershed splits at the waist between two objects; the gradient watershed splits where the image itself has an edge, which is what separates touching objects that have a visible boundary but no waist
params.label: Instances

params.help: What splits touching objects. The peaks of the distance map; only the peaks that stand clear of their surroundings (fewer false splits); or the centres of the blobs the image itself shows, found over a range of sizes, which is the one that copes with objects of different sizes
params.label: Seeds

params.help: Distance maxima: minimum distance between seeds
params.label: Seed distance

params.help: H-maxima: how far a peak must stand above its surroundings to be its own object; raise it when one object is split, lower it when two are merged
params.label: Seed depth

params.help: Blob centres: the smallest object radius to look for, in x / y pixels
params.label: Object radius

params.help: Blob centres: the largest radius; the detector answers to every size in between
params.label: Object radius max

params.help: Blob centres: how many sizes are tried between the two radii
params.label: Blob scales

params.help: Drop objects larger than this (0 = off): the usual way to remove a merged clump
params.label: Max. voxels

params.help: Drop objects that fill less than this fraction of their bounding box (0 = off): removes scattered debris
params.label: Min. fill

params.help: Drop objects whose bounding box is longer than this many times its width (0 = off)
params.label: Max. elongation

params.help: Grow every object outwards into the background by this much, nearest object first. Closes the gap an opening or a watershed line left, without letting two objects meet (0 = off)
params.label: Expand labels

params.help: Replace every object with the line down its middle: one voxel thick, the same length and the same topology. The centreline of a filament, and what its length is measured on
params.label: Centrelines

params.help: Objects touching the x / y edge are cut off, so their shape and size are not measurable
params.label: Drop border objects

params.help: Random walker fills outwards from seeds and stops where the image changes, so it copes with a boundary too weak or too broken for a threshold. The geodesic active contour is driven by edges, where the Classical step's Chan-Vese is driven by regions. The superpixels over-segment into pieces to merge or measure. The compact watershed pulls its regions towards round shapes
params.label: Method

params.help: The rough foreground the seeded methods start from; 0 asks the worker for an Otsu cut
params.label: Threshold

params.help: Random walker and compact watershed: how far a peak of the distance map must stand above its surroundings to seed its own object
params.label: Seed depth

params.help: Random walker: how strongly an intensity step stops the walk. Higher follows faint boundaries, lower lets the regions spread past them
params.label: Diffusion stiffness

params.help: Geodesic active contour: how many times the contour is moved
params.label: Contour steps

params.help: Geodesic active contour: positive inflates the contour, negative deflates it, 0 lets the edges alone decide
params.label: Balloon

params.help: Geodesic active contour: how sharply the edge map falls off at a gradient
params.label: Edge sharpness

params.help: Smoothing before the gradient (also Felzenszwalb's own smoothing)
params.label: Edge σ

params.help: SLIC: roughly how many pieces to cut the volume into
params.label: Superpixels

params.help: SLIC and the compact watershed: how much the pieces are pulled towards round shapes rather than following the intensity
params.label: Compactness

params.help: Felzenszwalb: larger merges more, so the pieces come out bigger
params.label: Merge scale

params.help: Felzenszwalb: pieces smaller than this are merged into a neighbour
params.label: Smallest piece

params.help: Objects larger than this × the median volume are flagged as possible merges
params.label: Size outlier factor

params.help: Built-in matches each frame to the next by optimal assignment on distance and overlap. btrack adds a motion model, so it holds identities through a crossing, and reconstructs lineages when cells divide; it runs in the Python worker
params.label: Tracker

params.help: How far an object may move between frames; the gate that keeps distant objects apart
params.label: Max. step

params.help: 0 matches on centroid distance alone, 1 on shared voxels alone; in between mixes them
params.label: Overlap weight

params.help: Frames an object may be missed for and still continue the same track (0 = never)
params.label: Close gaps

params.help: Tracks seen in fewer frames than this are dropped
params.label: Min. track length

params.help: Give every object of a track the track's id, so one object keeps one colour over time
params.label: Relabel by track

params.help: btrack only: a tracker configuration JSON; empty uses btrack's packaged cell configuration, which is fetched and cached on first use
params.label: btrack config

params.help: btrack only: run the global hypothesis optimisation, which is what links a mother to its daughters
params.label: Reconstruct lineages
